preamble: Labial palatalization of [b] to the voiced palatal stop [ɟ] before front vowels is a regional Eastern Romance feature. In the Moldavian dialect of Daco-Romanian the labials [p, b, m] before front vowels are realized as [c, ɟ, ɲ], so that standard bine 'well' is pronounced ghine; it is a well-known stereotype of Moldavian speech but is absent from standard Romanian. Aromanian shows the same outcome lexicalized in ghini 'well' from Latin bene, spelled with ⟨gh⟩ = /ɟ/. Other Daco-Romanian dialects (Crișana, Maramureș) palatalize [b] to the cluster [bdʲ] instead.

examples.note: Before front vowels the labials [p, b, m] are palatalized and become [c, ɟ, ɲ] in Moldavian speech (also picior > k'icior 'leg', miere > n'ere 'honey'); Wikipedia transcribes the bine example as [ˈɡʲini].
Aromanian ⟨gh⟩ stands for /ɟ/ before e and i; Wiktionary transcribes the word as [ˈɡi.ni]. The parallel voiceless change appears in cheptu 'chest' from Latin pectus.
